finding: Meta-analysis of Chinese RCTs: combined acupuncture plus moxibustion had higher total effective rate than herbal medicine or western medicine; evidence quality likely low.
Urine GC-MS metabolites in a restraint-stress rat model of CFS before/after exercise; steroid hormone biosynthesis and sphingolipid pathways altered.
note: Animal stress model, not human ME/CFS

finding: ME/CFS patients with abnormal exercise test results had more frequent and severe PEM, worse function and more bedbound status than those with normal results.
Commentary arguing PACE safety data do not exclude harm from graded activity therapies, given poor fitness change (non-adherence) and patient reports of deterioration.
Serum activin B was elevated in CFS/ME vs controls and reference interval; activin A, follistatin and routine pathology were normal.
note: Small, no n in abstract, not replicated

finding: Full mtDNA sequencing of 93 UK/South African CFS patients found no clinically proven pathogenic mtDNA mutations.
Finnish registry baseline incidence in girls 11-15 pre HPV vaccination: 0.53/100,000 for CFS/SEID, 4.21 for POTS.
ME/CFS with comorbid fibromyalgia reported more frequent and severe muscle and general PEM symptoms and worse physical function.
Discussion paper comparing CBT for paediatric CFS/ME and depression.
Adolescents with CFS had lower baseline HRV (RMSSD) than healthy, and failed to show HRV reduction or skin conductance recovery after a social stress task.
A restrictive homebound IOM-based research definition selected more impaired and symptomatic patients than the broader IOM criteria.
Low problem-solving confidence associated with higher odds of CFS (about 5x) and ISF classification.
After submaximal exercise, relations between autonomic recovery and pain change were examined; ME/CFS autonomic-pain relationships differed from controls (only moderate correlations).
12 weeks graded or intermittent exercise increased NK cell LAMP-1/2 expression and aerobic capacity vs usual care; no CD8+CD38+ change.

n: 257 mixed (back pain, widespread pain, FM, ME/CFS)
finding: Pacing themes had mixed associations: activity consistency linked to less fatigue and better function, activity adjustment to more fatigue and lower function.
Anxiety 42.2%, depression 33.3% and clinically significant health anxiety 42.2% in CFS/ME service patients.
Hypothesis: EBV-infected ectopic lymphoid aggregates in nervous tissue drive neuroinflammation in ME/CFS.
Qualitative study: recovered people remain in a persistent liminal state between illness and wellness, continuing pacing and rest.
Ventricular CSF lactate by 1H MRSI was higher in CFS, FM and CFS+FM than controls, with no difference among patient groups.
note: Pooled from two studies; not CFS-specific

finding: Narrative review proposing neuroinflammation and glial activation (spinal/postural pain signalling plus neurotropic infection) as ME/CFS etiopathology.
CFS and FM had longer reaction time at gait initiation than controls (p=0.004, p=0.001); no group differences on Purdue Pegboard.

n: 15 CFS, 5 ICF, 9 other fatigue, 10 recovered; 20 exposed + 10 unexposed controls
finding: No differences in Giardia-specific CD4 activation, proliferation or cytokines between fatigue groups; sCD40L raised in post-infectious fatigue and correlated with fatigue.
Latent class analysis of PACE baseline data defined five subgroups (core 33%, mood 21%, functional somatic 21%, many symptoms 14%, avoidant-inactive 11%).
Systematic review: insufficient evidence for diet or supplements; fatigue improved with NADH, probiotics, cocoa polyphenol chocolate, NADH+CoQ10.
Prevalence of chronic disabling fatigue rose from 1.47% at 13 to 2.99% at 18; about 75% not classified at next time point, 8% persistent through adolescence.
Retrospective ratings suggested higher pre-morbid perfectionism, self-sacrifice and stress in CFS.
Patients and GPs identified lack of a central coordinator and need for education in CFS care.
Meta-ethnography of children's experience: disruption, uncertainty, disbelief, role of diagnosis and supportive relationships.
Phenomenological study of men's experience of CFS/ME and occupational impact.
Healthcare professionals report contested legitimacy and emotional burden working with CFS/ME.
Russian trial of intravenous placenta extract (laennec) reported reduced fatigue and improved VO2 vs controls.
note: Small, unclear blinding, no placebo stated

finding: Noophen reduced MFI-20 fatigue in cerebrovascular disease patients with fatigue.
Medical education module on ME/CFS evaluation improved students' knowledge and empathy.
CDC Grand Rounds introduction on CFS terminology and research.
Decision-tree analysis of DePaul Symptom Questionnaire separated MS from ME/CFS 81.2% of the time, with flu-like symptoms and tender nodes most discriminating.
Random peptide microarray immunosignature of 25 peptides separated ME cases from controls; peptides matched human self-antigens and endogenous retroviral sequences.
Poorer sleep quality was associated with higher IL-1b (p=0.043), IL-6 (p=0.033) and TNF-a (p=0.044) and greater fatigue severity.
Baduanjin Qigong vs waitlist reduced anxiety/depression and raised plasma adiponectin.
Philosophical paper applying epistemic injustice to patient testimony in healthcare encounters.
Flinders Fatigue Scale validated; CFS/ME and insomnia scored higher than OSA and volunteers; cut-offs for fatigue severity set.
Tregs and CD4+ iNKT percentage were increased in CFS/ME vs healthy controls; no abnormality common to CFS/ME and MS.
Self-reported CFS was more frequent in myofascial than non-myofascial TMD (19% vs 5%, p=.01).
CFS participants showed attentional bias to fatigue words, somatic interpretation bias and poorer attentional control than controls.
TRPM3 receptor expression reduced on unstimulated CD56bright NK cells in CFS/ME; Ca2+ flux responses to PregS were altered/increased rather than reduced.
About two-thirds reported positive GP continuity of care.
CFS group more fatigued, distressed, with more sleep disturbance than rheumatic disease groups; different cognitive-behavioural response profiles.
CFS classification at 17 raised odds of chronic widespread pain (OR 3.87, 95% CI 2.05-7.31); females about twice as likely to have either.
Targeted SNP study of TRP, cholinergic and adrenergic genes: 60 nominal SNPs; ADRA1A rs2322333 higher in CFS/ME (45.3% vs 23.4%) but p=0.059 after correction.
Experience sampling: fatigue and pain predicted subsequent activity limitation; wellness predicted all-or-nothing behaviour.

n: 25 ME/CFS vs 13 Lyme vs 11 SLE vs 25 HC
finding: Plasma RNA metagenomics found very low microbial content; differences between groups were explained by contamination and batch effects.
Partners/parents of CFS/ME patients showed moderate to high distress in most studies.
Visual-probe studies consistently show attentional bias to health threat words in CFS; interpretive bias found with elaborative tasks.
Young people thought CFS/ME caused depression, with a cyclical relationship.
Privacy on online forums is contextual; users manage self-presentation.
CFS group scored lower on 5 of 6 psychological well-being dimensions than matched controls.
Reported age at death in a convenience sample was earlier than US norms for all-cause (55.9 y) and cardiovascular (58.8 y) mortality.
No study tested treatment for paediatric CFS/ME with depression; evidence on effective approach absent.
POTS prevalence on active stand was 5.7% in CFS vs 6.9% non-CFS adults (p=0.54); 18.2% vs 17.4% in adolescents; POTS not a discriminating marker.
note: Fukuda-type CFS, active stand not tilt; control group is fatigued patients

finding: Single exercise bout increased fatigue in ME/CFS vs controls (mean delta 0.73, 95% CI 0.24-1.23), larger when measured 4 h or more after exercise.
Interval and continuous exercise of matched work produced similar symptom exacerbation over 4 days in moderately affected CFS.
CFS had worse observer-rated emotional awareness and more difficulty identifying emotions than controls.
TRPV1 modulators reversed behavioural changes in a swim-stress rat model of CFS.
ASL-fMRI during fatiguing cognitive task: CFS had weaker increase in static FC (insula-temporo-occipital, precuneus-thalamus/striatum) and lower dynamic hippocampal FC; correlated with task fatigue.
Salivary ATP synthase beta and aconitase were upregulated in CFS (replicated by western blot), MDH2 not confirmed; discovered in one twin pair.
Lower putamen activity during low-reward condition in childhood CFS, correlated with fatigue severity.
Single moderate cycling bout worsened fatigue (ES 1.17) but leucocyte expression of 19 genes did not change; FCN1 and P2RX4 higher in CFS overall.
Obesity prevalence higher in adolescents attending specialist services (OR 2.31 at 13y, 4.07 at 16y) than ALSPAC non-CFS.
Adolescent CFS patients less able to engage left amygdala and mid-posterior insula during emotional conflict, related to fatigue severity.
Cluster analysis found two personality profiles among FM/CFS patients, not related to severity.
DePaul Symptom Questionnaire PEM subscale discriminated patients from controls and had better psychometrics than MFI-20 and SF-36.
Infectious mononucleosis registered in 11.1% of CFS/ME children in prior 2 years vs 0.5% comparators; more depression, anxiety, migraine, muscle pain, infections in primary care.
eLORETA EEG showed reduced alpha source density and hypoconnectivity in CEN, salience and default mode networks in ME.
12 weeks graded or intermittent exercise improved CD4 lymphocyte activation and VO2peak without worsening symptoms; baseline CD3/CD4 activation markers lower in CFS than controls.
note: Same cohort as the NK paper, pilot

finding: M-wave muscle fatigue, oxidative stress markers (TBARS, ascorbate) and CD26 on PBMC examined with history of stressors and quality of life.
Global grey matter volume did not differ between CFS and controls; pain, not fatigue, predicted left DLPFC GMV and NAA/Cr.
92 of 528 protein kinase genes differentially expressed in NK cells of severe CFS/ME vs controls (37 up, 55 down).
Factor analysis suggests PEM comprises two constructs: generalised and muscle-specific fatigue.
Serum BAFF was elevated in ME/CFS (p=0.011); APRIL unchanged; no T-cell subset change with rituximab; lower baseline IgG in responders (p=0.03).
note: Post hoc analysis of Norwegian trials

finding: Schisandra polysaccharide altered urinary metabolites in a rat stress model of CFS.
Retrospective reports of pregnancy, abuse, mobbing, car accident and economic problems were associated with CFS onset.
Sequencing of AMPD1, CPT2 and PYGM found no genotype differences from controls or association with severity.
Adolescents with CFS/ME described eating difficulties from abdominal symptoms, fatigue and taste/smell changes.
COMT high-activity homozygotes on clonidine had worse step counts (2500 fewer), sleep and quality of life vs placebo (interaction p=0.04, 0.003, 0.018).
Photo-narrative study of how places shape illness experience in ME.
Gait-initiation balance control (tauG K value) was worse in CFS (0.55) and FM (0.57) than controls (0.50).

population: Unexplained fatigue / CFS/ME in primary care
finding: GP-oriented review on diagnosing CFS/ME with clinical criteria and normal routine tests.
SF-36 subscales captured substantial activity reduction and discriminated patients from controls.
Passive straight leg raise (neuromuscular strain) vs sham increased pain, concentration difficulty, composite symptoms during and 24 h after in CFS (composite P=0.005 at 24 h).
Clinicians working with paediatric CFS/ME describe working with uncertainty.
Three FM/ME patients with severe exacerbations reported relief with oxygen therapy.
Prevalence of BPD in CFS 1.8-17% across five studies; association unclear.
Long-term methylphenidate: 34.7% still taking; of those, 48% reported at least 50% fatigue improvement and 62% concentration improvement.
KIR genotypes and alleles did not differ between CFS/ME and controls apart from lower frequency of telomeric A/B motif (P<0.05).
ME/CFS forum users trust peers with similar experience while valuing biomedical advice.
Review: no proposed aetiological factor strongly reproducible; CBT and GET described as moderately effective.
CBT effect sizes were larger in NL than UK (fatigue d 1.74 vs 0.99; physical functioning 0.99 vs 0.33).
CAM use reported by 70% of PACE participants; not associated with clinically important outcomes.
Primary care resources for CFS/ME were beneficial but poorly implemented (47% of patients not given info pack).
31% (17/55) met criteria for cow's milk protein intolerance; they had worse quality of life at baseline, not at 6 months on milk-free diet.
TRPM3 surface expression reduced on CD19+ B cells and CD56bright NK cells in CFS/ME, with reduced cytoplasmic calcium after stimulation.
French narrative review of CFS and the SEID concept.
Systematic review of drug RCTs: twenty drug classes tested, ten shown slightly to moderately effective; no drug recommended.
Of 535 diagnosed patients, 30.3% met Fukuda, 32.0% met Fukuda and ICC; 78.6% female; common prior events cold/flu, GI illness, stress.
CFS showed higher electrodermal responses during distressing film, linked to post-task fatigue increase; lower observer-rated emotion expression.
note: Sympathetic arousal measured by skin conductance

finding: CBT and GET effect on sleep inconsistent across eight studies.
Adolescent CFS had higher plasma norepinephrine, epinephrine and FT4 and lower urine cortisol/creatinine than controls.
Path analysis: poor sleep quality directly related to physical and mental quality of life without mediation by fatigue.

population: Gulf War vs OEF/OIF veterans, CFS
finding: 17.6% of OEF/OIF veterans met CFS criteria; worse mental function than Desert Storm veterans with CFS.
Housebound patients (about one quarter) were more impaired in function, PEM, autonomic, neuroendocrine and immune symptoms.
Longitudinal MRI showed greater white matter volume loss in left inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus in CFS.
Older patients with long illness duration reported better mental health; younger long-duration group had worse autonomic and immune symptoms.
MAPK signalling in NK cells altered: ERK1/2 reduced in CD56dim, MEK1/2 and p38 raised in CD56bright after K562 stimulation.
Qualitative themes on psychological impact of physical dependency.

population: Mouse LPS plus swim stress model
finding: NLRP3 inflammasome activation in diencephalon in LPS/swim mouse fatigue model; NLRP3 KO altered response.
Quality of care rated poor by 60.6% (primary), 47.7% (specialist), 71.2% (coordination).
Subjective but not actigraphy-defined sleep predicted next-day fatigue; presleep arousal predicted poor perceived sleep.
Melatonin lowered plasma lipid hydroperoxides in MS patients with fatigue.
NK lysis lower in ME/CFS (17% vs 31%); 11 SNPs in TRPC4, TRPC2, TRPM3, TRPM8 and AChR genes found in NK cells.
BP and HR from 24-h monitoring showed abnormal correlations with MRI in brainstem vasomotor centre, midbrain and hypothalamus in CFS, without group MRI differences.
Two ways of applying 1994 criteria agreed on 44 of 86 cases (kappa 0.63); cases by both methods were more impaired.
34 miRNAs raised in PBMC; four validated (miR-99b, miR-330, miR-126, miR-30c), strongest in NK cells in an independent cohort.
Discriminating cytokines shifted with illness duration: IL-1a higher in recent adolescents, IL-8 high early but opposite after 2 years; classification 75-88%.
Five Minute Speech Sample moderately agreed with Camberwell Family Interview for expressed emotion.
Review: primary sleep disorders common and need exclusion in CFS.
SNP chip GWAS found 442 candidate SNPs (adjusted P<0.05) incl. two missense and a cluster in T-cell receptor loci.
note: Small sample; DecodeME later found different loci

finding: Only 13.2% of referred patients met CFS/ME; 46.3% received mental and behavioural diagnoses.
After 12-week graded activity with cognitive training, objective and subjective neurocognitive performance improved; no controls.
Commentary arguing SEID should not replace ME and CFS; criteria more heterogeneous.
CBT improved fatigue in both ethnic groups.
Sociological concept paper on illness as identity work.
EEG mapping showed raised delta, theta and alpha1 energy and reduced nonlinear dynamics in CFS.
note: Control group unclear (other outpatients), Chinese study

finding: mtDNA sequencing: no pathogenic mutations or SNP association with case status; haplogroups J, U, H and 8 SNPs associated with symptoms.
Sex-specific associations between Firmicutes (Clostridium, Streptococcus, Lactobacillus, Enterococcus) and symptoms.
CD127 and PSGL-1 reduced on CD8+ T cell subsets in CFS/ME.
Long-term management themes of awareness, acceptance, connection.
CD57 and perforin co-expression raised on CD56dim NK cells in CFS/ME, suggesting increased NK differentiation.
Online group study of identity crisis in CFS/ME.
Thesis on muscle cell energy metabolism in CFS/ME myoblasts, including pH and DCA effects.
CFS had smaller fusion amplitudes and convergence/accommodation deficits vs controls.
Thesis comparing autonomic and cognitive symptoms across CFS criteria sets and overlap with depression.
Blood cell ATP was higher in CFS, mitochondrial cristae more condensed; ETC complex activities, membrane potential intact; extra ATP from non-mitochondrial sources.
Cognitive-behavioural beliefs and behaviours compared across CFS/ME and IBS.
Leukocyte gene expression factors (purinergic/cellular modulators; nociception/stress) were higher in CFS and lower with depression severity.
Negative responses from significant others linked to same-moment symptom severity and distress.
Latent class analysis gave polysymptomatic, oligosymptomatic and pain-only phenotypes; polysymptomatic more severe and with more comorbidity.
Self-critical perfectionism predicted blunted cortisol response to TSST; lower cortisol reactivity linked to greater symptom severity.
Secondary analysis of RCT: no therapist effects and no influence of therapeutic alliance on outcome.
Hypothesis review proposing ME/CFS is a contagious infectious disease based on outbreaks.
Fatigue described as post-exertional, fluctuating, multidimensional.
Hypothesis paper on hippocampus role in ME/CFS pathogenesis.
Patients meeting Canadian research criteria were more impaired than those meeting IOM clinical criteria.
Describes a multi-stage community prevalence study design for paediatric CFS/ME.
21-32% of CFS patients reported TMD; 0-43% of TMD patients reported CFS; limited evidence.
ME/CFS had higher Pattern Glare scores at mid spatial frequency than controls.
Children presented differently from adults: fewer cognitive symptoms, more equal sex ratio; adolescents more headache, depression.
PCC seeded resting-state connectivity increased to dorsal and rostral ACC in CFS, correlated with fatigue; lower global efficiency.
CAM-only users had better social functioning than traditional-only or combined users.
Migraine associated with 1.5-fold higher CFS risk (52.72 vs 28.85 per 10,000 person-years).
5-HTTLPR short-allele genotypes (SS, SLG) predicted fewer steps/day and higher disability at 30 weeks.
CFS plus FM had more disability, pain and cognitive complaints and improved more slowly than CFS alone.
Conceptual model of outcomes mattering to children: fluctuating symptoms, activity, participation, emotional well-being.
Qigong reduced fatigue and improved quality of life vs control in bereaved CFS-like participants.
During CBT pain and fatigue decreased together; symptom focusing and physical functioning explained 4-14% of pain change.
NR3C1-1F promoter methylation lower in CFS than controls (CpG_1.5 survived Bonferroni, p=0.0014) and correlated with post-dexamethasone salivary cortisol.
Patients prioritised understanding disease processes, treatments and diagnosis for research.
Siblings had higher anxiety than norms; depression and quality of life similar.
Factor analysis of DePaul Symptom Questionnaire: PEM, cognitive, sleep, and combined neuroendocrine/autonomic/immune domains.
Cochrane review: exercise therapy reduced fatigue vs passive/no treatment at end of treatment.
note: Oxford/CDC-era trials, risk of bias, no PEM-defined

finding: On bad days vs good days: higher resting HR, 21% could not stand 10 min, 43% developed POT only on bad days; LV end-diastolic diameter and stroke volume index lower on bad days.
Severe CFS/ME showed longitudinal changes in iNKT phenotypes, naive CD8+ T, gamma-delta T and NK receptors over 6 months.
Childhood CFS recruited wider frontal areas (MFG, dACC) during dual task, linked to motivation and fatigue.
Serum IL-7, IL-8 and IFN-g higher in severe; IL-6 lower in moderate than HC; cytokine patterns differ by severity.
Current IQ in CFS adolescents lower than expected from school level and pre-CFS achievement; controls showed no discrepancy.
Fatigue and Energy Scale captured post-exertional fatigue exacerbation after both physical exercise and driving simulation.
In CFS+FM, impaired pain inhibition (CPM) associated with worse cognitive inhibition; self-reported pain linked to reaction time in CFS-only.
Hypothesis paper on ketogenic diet, fasting and caloric restriction as mitoprotective in ME/CFS.
Patients view pacing as multifaceted; four behavioural typologies identified.
COMT, FKBP5 and CRHR1 SNP frequencies did not differ between CFS and controls; COMT Met/Met linked to higher cortisol, lower IgG3, higher IgE and recurrent respiratory infections.
Men were 9.1% of CFS cohort, younger onset, less pain, fewer muscle/immune symptoms; fibromyalgia 29% vs 58%.
QFS and CFS patients equally fatigued; no difference in inflammatory markers; QFS less often female, more physically active.
KPAX002 (methylphenidate plus nutrients) lowered CIS fatigue by 36.4 points (34%) at 12 weeks (p<0.0001); 87% had at least 25% decrease.
EQ-5D-3L mean 0.47 vs population 0.85; adjusted disutility -0.29.
Post-LPS depressive-like state in mice with raised brain TNF and 5-HT2A receptor mRNA.
Adolescent CFS had 44 points lower overall PedsQL HRQOL than controls.
SEID criteria captured 88% of samples vs 92% Fukuda; a four-item empiric definition selected a more impaired group.
Case of maternal-inherited mitochondrial myopathy initially diagnosed CFS, responding to riboflavin and thiamine.
Atopy associated with higher CFS incidence (1.37 vs 0.87 per 1000 PY; adjusted HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.30-1.69).
CFS associated with organic erectile dysfunction (adjusted HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.26-2.81).
Immune/inflammation SNP chip: 32 SNPs associated with CFS including complement genes CFB (rs4151667) and CFH (rs1061170) and IL18 UTR.
SEID criteria also classified many with major depression and other illnesses; community prevalence rose 2.8-fold vs Fukuda.
33.1% had childhood trauma; 47.6% had a personality disorder.
Fluorescent nanodiamonds used to trace alum adjuvant particles; macrophagic myofasciitis mentioned.
ADCLS and CFS had similar phenotype and cytokines; no confirmed Lyme serology in ADCLS.
Facial image feature classification reached about 88% accuracy for CFS prediction.
Brucella antigen injections in mice produced low wheel running and, at a high dose, transient anaemia.
Bayesian joint SNP model predicted CFS status with 80% ten-fold cross-validated accuracy.
IPA of parent-carers of severely ill ME patients: identity change, guilt, uncertainty.
Behavioural interventions with graded activity: small to medium effects (g 0.25-0.66; fatigue 0.61-0.66) at post-treatment and follow-up; some publication bias.
Altered NK receptors and adhesion molecules and CD4/CD8 T cell receptors, differing by severity.
NIH P2P review: eight case definitions in use; no validated diagnostic method; self-report scales differentiate from controls only in research settings.
NIH P2P review: rintatolimod low-strength benefit in 2 trials; counselling and GET improved fatigue in some trials; others inconclusive.
NIH Pathways to Prevention workshop process description and research gaps.
Critical editorial opposing replacement of ME and CFS by SEID.
NIRS during handgrip: ME/CFS had smaller dO2Hb and dHHb, higher RPE, lower TTI; differences diminished after adjusting for TTI and tHb.
Occurrence rates of PEM, unrefreshing sleep and neurocognitive deficits varied widely across studies.
Argues for operationalising essential features to separate ME from CFS.
CFS prevalence 1.3%; CFS had more mood (OR 1.72-5.42) and anxiety disorders than FM and IBS.
Cassia fistula extract reduced immobility in forced swim mouse 'CFS' model.
Activity Pacing Questionnaire reduced to 26 items with five themes.
Patients on weekly or more B12 injections with oral folic acid: good responders used more frequent injections.
note: Survey of treated patients, no control

finding: CBT and GET equally reduced fatigue and anxiety/depression in routine care; metacognition change predicted fatigue.
Simulation: reduced mitochondrial ATP synthesis capacity leads to depleted adenine nucleotide pool, prolonged recovery, worse with repeated exercise.
After handgrip, forearm occlusion trapping metabolites increased fatigue ratings in CFS (p=0.04) with heat and mechanical hyperalgesia; indirect evidence for peripheral muscle metabolite sensing.
Case report of yoga-based lifestyle intervention improving well-being and personality.
Canadian Consensus Criteria subgrouping showed no differences in disease markers or 30-week prognosis, except digit span backward.
Significant-other beliefs and solicitous/negative responses associated with patient distress and symptom severity.
Partner solicitous responses and patient relationship dissatisfaction predicted less improvement after CBT.
Earlier onset age correlated with autoimmunity in patients and relatives.
German medical-certification commentary on CFS, neurasthenia and somatoform coding.
Traditional Chinese medicine theory linking bladder meridian to CFS.
48.5% had personality disorders; associated with more depressive symptoms.
Self-reported diagnosed CFS 1.4% and FM 1.5%; comorbid 0.3%; poorer health status especially with both.
T1w signal in prefrontal and thalamic white matter rose with CFS severity (independent of mood), suggesting upregulated myelination.
Hypothesis that CFS is persistent burnout with HPA axis dysregulation.
Participants differentiated tiredness, fatigue and exhaustion (after overexertion); pacing and rest used to adapt.
Sleep seen as central, variable, and linked to daytime functioning.
Describes PACE design and main result that CBT and GET outperformed APT and SMC on self-rated fatigue and function.
Mediation analysis: fear-avoidance beliefs were the largest mediator of CBT and GET effects; exercise tolerance mediated GET.
Jujube polysaccharide improved behaviour and antioxidant/immune markers in a rat stress model.

population: CFS vs primary insomnia vs good sleepers
finding: Both CFS and insomnia had lower central ultra-slow power during slow wave sleep; CFS had normal or longer SWS duration.
Overview of mixed-methods research programme in ME/CFS.
Daytime napping, especially afternoon, associated with poorer cognition and more sleepiness; wake after sleep onset predicted fatigue.
DePaul Symptom Questionnaire showed good to excellent test-retest reliability.
Sudden-onset ME criteria identified more functionally impaired patients with more severe PEM than CFS criteria.

population: ME/CFS (CDC) vs chronic fatigue vs controls
finding: CD8+CD38+ and CD8+HLA-DR+ proportions higher in ME/CFS; CD19+ and CD4/CD8 ratio lower; no link to severity or O&NS/leaky gut markers.
Empirically selected core symptoms (fatigue, PEM, neurocognitive, unrefreshing sleep) best discriminated patients from controls.
Cluster analysis defined a Neuro-Inflammatory and Oxidative Fatigue subgroup validated by IgM to gut LPS, O&NS epitopes, IL-1 and neopterin.
Review of TLR-mediated innate immunity in CFS/ME as a potential therapeutic target.
PEM classification depends on item wording in self-report criteria.

population: CFS/ME vs fatigued breast cancer survivors
finding: CFS/ME had more fatigue interference and depressed mood than fatigued cancer survivors.
Case study exploring stamina versus fatigue for case definitions.
Psychosocial thesis on self-experience of ME.
Lifelong fatigue was rarely definable and few differences by it; recommends dropping it as exclusion.
Current work activity best operationalised substantial activity reduction, correlating with SF-36 and actigraphy.
Facebook group use in CFS/ME (thesis).
Thesis: GET may improve sleep in CFS when delivered by experienced therapists; evidence for CBT limited.
Timed loaded standing endurance lower in CFS than nondisabled controls (p<0.001) and than older osteoporotic women.
Gait automaticity reduced: 55.9% of CFS stopped walking on dual task vs 5.3% controls.
CFS and insomnia groups similar on subjective sleep and cognitions; both worse than controls.
Longitudinal mediation modelling in PACE trial: methodological design considerations.
